newsitem.title: USA: Ex-publisher sues Disney over dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Ex-publisher sues Disney over dismissal.

text.p: Former Fort Worth Star-Telegram publisher Richard Connor filed a lawsuit against Walt Disney Co, the corporate parent of the paper that dismissed him, Connor's attorney said.

Disney, ABC Inc, ABC senior vice president Phillip Meek and Capital Cities/ABC president Robert Iger were named as defendants in the suit that alleges libel, slander and interference with Connor's contract, Connor's attorney, Frank Branson, said in a statement.
Disney representatives were not immediately available for comment.
Connor is seeking "reasonable damages" not to exceed former president Michael Ovitz's $90 million severance package, Branson said.
In the complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Wichita Falls, Texas, Connor had opted not to step down as publisher of the Forth Worth Star-Telegram when offered a severance package, Branson said.
Connor learned of his firing by reading the paper when it named his replacement, Branson said.
Connor accused the ABC executives of alleged scheming for his dismissal, while providing assurances that he was secure in his job, Branson said.
